native_result.HypoA: Symbolic capital components such as house size, the number of daggers, and hatchets/swords are characterized by negative values on the first principal component (PC1) and exhibit a wide distribution of values on the second principal component (PC2). This Principal component analysis (PCA) is on the forms of capital. The values of the individual elements of the forms of capital form the attributes.
native_result.HypoB: In the 100-year-sliced PCA of the capital matrix, the symbolic-capital components HouseSize (Zhausgr), Dagger (ZDolch) and HatchetSword (ZAxtSchwert) behave as a SINGLE COHERENT BLOCK on PC1 and SEPARATE INTO A BIPOLAR CONTRAST on PC2, with the 39 per-slice PC2 scores centred close to zero. PC1 absorbs 54.4% of the variance of the symbolic submatrix (PC2 adds 28.8%, together 83.2%); all three symbolic variables load with the same positive sign on PC1 - Dagger +0.662 (dominant), HouseSize +0.568, HatchetSword +0.489 - giving high PC1 scores to the late-Neolithic / Old-Bronze-Age slices (PC1 max +3.35 at BCE 1800 LN, +2.69 at BCE 1300 OBA) and low PC1 scores to the early-Neolithic slices (BCE 4300-3900 at -1.37). On PC2 (sign-normalised so that HatchetSword, the dominant-loading symbolic variable, is positive), HatchetSword loads +0.791, HouseSize loads -0.609, and Dagger loads -0.061 - i.e. after their shared PC1 movement is removed the triad splits into a HatchetSword-vs-HouseSize contrast while Dagger is essentially neutral. The 39 per-slice PC2 scores span min -1.55, q1 -0.41, median -0.13, q3 +0.51, max +2.45 (skew +0.81): a long right tail driven by OBA BCE 1500-1600 at +2.45, a lower tail from En/Mn BCE 3500-3400 at -1.55, and an interquartile range clustered near zero, so PC2 is best described as a residual axis on which the symbolic triad is only weakly separated. Compatibility check from the full 12-capital PCA (PC1 = 31.8%, PC2 = 20.4%) - the symbolic triad still all load positively on the global PC1 (Zhausgr +0.228, ZDolch +0.279, ZAxtSchwert +0.301) - independently confirms the coherent-block reading.
